title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in an urban environment during a major public event without apparent contingency for extreme traffic disruption. When fireworks celebrations created unexpected gridlock at the Golden Gate Bridge, multiple vehicles became trapped in congestion that drained their batteries faster than anticipated. The system was used in conditions outside what it was built or tested for, leaving at least a dozen vehicles stranded and requiring towing.

This is a failure of deployment planning rather than of the autonomous driving system itself. The company operated in San Francisco on a day when traffic patterns were predictably disrupted by a known major event, but did not withdraw service or position vehicles to avoid long idle periods in congestion. A human decision to restrict or redeploy the fleet during the Fourth of July festivities would have prevented the stranding.

Whether Waymo's system is sufficiently resilient to high-temperature conditions near fireworks, as indicated by one vehicle catching fire, is not established from the reporting.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic following a fireworks display at the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets with some requiring towing. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion in the area.

The incident also involved a Waymo vehicle that caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported. One passenger described the vehicle continuing to drive during the chaos when fireworks were being set off nearby. The company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions, while Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated it will hold conversations with public and private partners to ensure smoother traffic management for future events.
